sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Environment settings template
sections.what: Lists each setting the AI service reads, with a placeholder or local default and a short note explaining what it controls.
sections.why: Likely reason: documents the setup so developers can configure the service without reading the code.
sections.watch_out: Copying this file as is leaves placeholder keys in place, so the service silently uses mock output.

summary: A template listing every setting the AI service reads, with placeholder values and local development defaults.
purpose: Shows a developer which environment variables to set when running the AI service.
why: Likely reason: lets new developers configure the service without reading the code, and keeps real keys out of the repository.
how: First it sets the environment name and log level. Then it sets the Redis cache address and the PostgreSQL database address. Next it lists the Groq key and model name, then the OpenAI key, model name, and temperature. Last it lists the Pinecone key and index name. Each entry has a short note.
inputs: Copied by a developer and filled in with real keys and addresses.
outputs: Values the service reads at startup.
risks: The default database password is a common local value and must not be used in any shared setup. The example Groq model differs from the code default. The OpenAI temperature setting is not used by the chatbot code, which sets its own value.
debug: If the wrong model is used, compare this file with the config file and with the environment on the running machine. If keys are missing, the service falls back to mock or demonstration output.
